scenario.note: Only one of Prod3, Prod4, or Prod5 may have any units sold; the rest must have zero sales.

At most one of Prod5, Prod4, or Prod3 can have positive sales. This is modeled as a logical rule requiring that at least one of the three products has zero sales, i.e., at most one has positive sales.

scenario.note: The condition links the production of Prod3 in June to a minimum stock level for Prod2. This is modeled as a rule on the sum of store for Prod2.
If any units are made in February, then sales of Prod4 in April must be at least 150. This is modeled as a rule that links make in Feb to sell of Prod4 in Apr via a conditional constraint.

Make in February is only permitted if sales of Prod4 in April are at least 150. This is modeled as a rule that enforces a conditional constraint on the make variable in Feb based on the sell variable in Apr for Prod4.
The rule enforces that in March, either no units are sold (0) or at least 4750 units are sold. This is a logical OR condition on the sum of sales in March.

scenario.note: The rule enforces that either no units are sold in March, or at least 4750 units are sold in March. This is modeled as a logical condition on the sell measure for March.
Only one unit of any product can be sold in any of the months April, May, or March. This rule applies per product, and is interpreted as a per-product, per-month cap on sales in those months.
